# Appendix {#sec-appendix}

## Plant Feature Columns {#sec-appendix-features}

@tbl-features lists every column extracted from the plant voltage signal
for one 30-second window, in the order of the three feature families
introduced in the Feature Engineering section. The 22 continuous columns
are the ones entering the correlation analysis; in the classification
design matrix they are accompanied by the six quality columns at the foot
of the table, which describe the state of the electrode signal rather
than its shape. Each of the 22 continuous columns appears in the dataset
twice, once on its original scale and once as a per-session robust
z-score carrying the suffix `_snorm` (@eq-snorm); the two representations
are never mixed within one model.

Two implementation details apply throughout. The time-domain and
signal-dynamics columns are computed after a zero-phase 46–54 Hz
band-stop filter removes mains interference, which on the recorded
sessions accounts for the majority of the raw signal's total power and
would otherwise dominate every amplitude statistic. The spectral columns,
by contrast, are computed from the unfiltered signal so that the Welch
spectrum reflects the true spectral content; for the same reason the band
powers stop at 30 Hz and no band covering the mains frequency is formed.

| Column | Family | Description |
|:-----------------------|:---------|:-------------------------------|
| `plant_mean` | Time | Mean voltage in the window |
| `plant_median` | Time | Median voltage |
| `plant_std` | Time | Standard deviation, retaining slow baseline drift |
| `plant_detrend_std` | Time | Standard deviation after linear detrending, i.e. fast fluctuation only |
| `plant_iqr` | Time | Interquartile range, $Q_{75} - Q_{25}$ |
| `plant_min` | Time | Minimum voltage |
| `plant_max` | Time | Maximum voltage |
| `plant_range` | Time | Maximum minus minimum |
| `plant_rms` | Time | Root mean square |
| `plant_zcr` | Time | Zero-crossing rate about the window mean |
| `bp_0_1` | Spectral | Welch band power, 0–1 Hz |
| `bp_1_5` | Spectral | Welch band power, 1–5 Hz |
| `bp_5_15` | Spectral | Welch band power, 5–15 Hz |
| `bp_15_30` | Spectral | Welch band power, 15–30 Hz |
| `band_power_sum` | Spectral | Sum of the four band powers |
| `ratio_bp1_5_bp5_15` | Spectral | Ratio of the 1–5 Hz to the 5–15 Hz band power |
| `ratio_bp1_5_total` | Spectral | Share of the 1–5 Hz band in the total band power |
| `spectral_entropy` | Spectral | Shannon entropy of the Welch spectrum, normalised to [0, 1] |
| `hjorth_activity` | Dynamics | Signal variance |
| `hjorth_mobility` | Dynamics | Mean-frequency proxy, from the variance of the first difference |
| `hjorth_complexity` | Dynamics | Frequency-change proxy, from the variance of the second difference |
| `spike_rate` | Dynamics | Share of samples deviating more than $3 \cdot \mathrm{MAD}$ from the window median |
| `plant_sat_pos_frac` | Quality | Share of samples at the upper ADC rail |
| `plant_sat_neg_frac` | Quality | Share of samples at the lower ADC rail |
| `plant_const_flag` | Quality | All samples in the window identical |
| `plant_quality` | Quality | Verdict: `ok`, `suspect_*`, or `dead_*` |
| `plant_dead_flag` | Quality | Derived from `plant_quality`: signal unusable |
| `plant_suspect_flag` | Quality | Derived from `plant_quality`: signal usable but degraded |

: Plant feature columns: features extracted from the plant voltage signal per 30-second window. The 22 continuous columns additionally exist in a session-normalised variant with the suffix `_snorm`. {#tbl-features tbl-colwidths="[33,13,54]"}

## Labeling Equations {#sec-appendix-labeling}

The equations below formalise the labeling procedure described in
@sec-labeling-algorithm. Throughout, $w$ indexes a non-overlapping
30-second window and the subscript $s$ marks a statistic computed over
all windows of the same session, which is what makes every threshold
relative to the individual participant rather than to an absolute scale.

**Valence from facial expression.** Frames are sampled at 5 Hz. Let $F_w$
be the sampled frames of window $w$ in which HSEmotion detected a face,
$v_i \in [-1, 1]$ the per-frame valence estimate and $c_i$ the model's
confidence in it. The window's valence is the confidence-weighted mean of
those estimates:

$$
\mathrm{val}_w \;=\; \operatorname{clip}\!\left(
  \sum_{i \in F_w} \frac{c_i}{\sum_{j \in F_w} c_j}\, v_i,\;
  -1,\; +1 \right)
$$ {#eq-fer-valence}

Weighting by confidence lets frames in which the face was clearly visible
dominate over frames the model itself rates as uncertain. A window is only
labeled if a face was found in at least half of its sampled frames:

$$
\mathrm{cov}_w \;=\; \frac{|F_w|}{n_w}\,,
\qquad \text{window excluded if } \mathrm{cov}_w < 0.5
$$ {#eq-coverage}

**Arousal from heart-rate variability.** Let $\mathrm{RR}_1, \dots,
\mathrm{RR}_{N_w}$ be the artifact-corrected R-R intervals in
milliseconds falling into window $w$. Two standard measures are computed
from them, the root mean square of successive differences and the mean
heart rate:

$$
\mathrm{RMSSD}_w \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{1}{N_w - 1}
  \sum_{i=1}^{N_w - 1}\left(\mathrm{RR}_{i+1} - \mathrm{RR}_i\right)^2}
$$ {#eq-rmssd}

$$
\overline{\mathrm{HR}}_w \;=\;
  \frac{60\,000}{\frac{1}{N_w}\sum_{i=1}^{N_w} \mathrm{RR}_i}
$$ {#eq-hr}

A window is excluded if it contains fewer than ten beats, or if more than
5 % of its beats had to be corrected. Both measures are then expressed as
robust z-scores against the session's own centre and spread, using the
median and the scaled median absolute deviation rather than mean and
standard deviation so that individual outlying windows cannot move the
reference:

$$
z_s(x) \;=\; \frac{x - \mathrm{med}_s(x)}{1.4826 \cdot \mathrm{MAD}_s(x)}
$$ {#eq-robust-z}

Because RMSSD falls with physiological activation while heart rate rises
with it, RMSSD is inverted before the two are averaged into one arousal
index:

$$
a_w \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\left(
  -\,z_s(\mathrm{RMSSD}_w) + z_s(\overline{\mathrm{HR}}_w)\right)
$$ {#eq-arousal}

**Deadbands.** Each axis receives a neutral deadband whose half-width is
derived from the spread of that axis' own values within the session:

$$
\tau_{\text{val}} = k \cdot 1.4826 \cdot \mathrm{MAD}_s(\mathrm{val}),
\quad
\tau_{\text{aro}} = k \cdot 1.4826 \cdot \mathrm{MAD}_s(a)
$$ {#eq-tau}

The multiplier is fixed at $k = 0.5$ for both axes, so the deadband spans
roughly one robust standard deviation in total. This value was selected
on a pilot session as the largest deadband that still left a substantial
share of windows with a directional label: raising it collapses the
dataset into the neutral class, lowering it labels windows whose
deviation from the participant's baseline is within their ordinary
resting fluctuation.

**Discretisation.** Both axes are discretised by the same rule, each
against its own median and its own deadband:

$$
d_w = \begin{cases}
\text{positive} & \text{if } \mathrm{val}_w >
  \mathrm{med}_s(\mathrm{val}) + \tau_{\text{val}} \\
\text{negative} & \text{if } \mathrm{val}_w <
  \mathrm{med}_s(\mathrm{val}) - \tau_{\text{val}} \\
\text{neutral}  & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-valence-class}

$$
l_w = \begin{cases}
\text{activated} & \text{if } a_w > \mathrm{med}_s(a) + \tau_{\text{aro}} \\
\text{calm}      & \text{if } a_w < \mathrm{med}_s(a) - \tau_{\text{aro}} \\
\text{neutral}   & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-arousal-class}

**Crossing into the emotion label.** The two axis labels are combined
into the final five-class label following the quadrant structure of the
circumplex model (@fig-circumplex). A window only receives a directional
label if both axes are directional:

$$
y_w = \begin{cases}
\text{neutral} & \text{if } d_w = \text{neutral}
  \ \lor\ l_w = \text{neutral} \\
(d_w,\, l_w)   & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-crossing}

so that $y_w$ takes one of the five values *negative calm*, *negative
activated*, *positive calm*, *positive activated*, or *neutral*.

**Session normalisation of the plant features.** The `_snorm`
representation of @tbl-features applies the same robust standardisation
as @eq-robust-z, but to each plant feature $x$ rather than to an HRV
measure:

$$
x^{\mathrm{snorm}}_w \;=\;
  \frac{x_w - \mathrm{med}_s(x)}{1.4826 \cdot \mathrm{MAD}_s(x)}
$$ {#eq-snorm}

This removes constant offsets between sessions, since electrode
placement, plant state, and ambient conditions differ from one recording
to the next, while preserving the within-session variation that the classifier
is meant to exploit.

## Example Session Record {#sec-appendix-session}

@fig-session-timeline documents one complete recording, session
`2026-07-06_19-51_proband_15`, as the labeling algorithm of
@sec-labeling-algorithm sees it. It is included as a worked example of a
session record: the same processing was applied unchanged to every
session, and this one is shown because it is a full-length recording
whose windows carry labels from all five classes.

The upper four panels hold the quantities the algorithm reads, each
plotted against the session median it is judged relative to, and the two
lower panels the labels it produces. Reading the figure downwards
therefore reproduces the order of the labeling procedure: the two HRV
measures, the two axis values derived from them and from the facial
video, the plant voltage that the classifier will later have to recover
these labels from, and finally the discretized axes and their crossing.
The plant voltage and the ambient CO~2~ trace share the fourth panel
because the correlation analysis of @sec-results tests exactly this pair
against each other.

![Example session record: the full ten-minute recording of session `2026-07-06_19-51_proband_15`, plotted on the non-overlapping 30-second window grid. From top: RMSSD; mean heart rate; the two quantities that decide the labels, FER valence on the left axis (green) and the HRV arousal index in robust z-units on the right axis (orange); the plant voltage (teal, left axis) with ambient CO~2~ overlaid (purple, right axis); the two per-axis labels; and the crossed five-class emotion label. Dotted horizontal lines mark the session medians each window is judged against (@eq-valence-class, @eq-arousal-class). The shaded band at the left and the dashed vertical line mark the 30-second baseline preceding the video. In the two label rows, light grey marks windows excluded rather than labeled, following @eq-coverage. The plant trace is decimated to 1 Hz for display only; the features of @tbl-features are computed on the undecimated signal.](figures/session_timeline.png){#fig-session-timeline width=90%}

Work sections, and @fig-live-dashboard the real-time component of

rather than contributing evidence for the hypotheses. That is why both

## Permutation Tests {#sec-appendix-permutation}

The three figures below document the permutation tests behind the
p-values reported in @sec-results, one per target variable and in the
order in which the targets are discussed there. Each test repeatedly
shuffles the labels, re-runs the complete participant-grouped five-fold
loop with the winning architecture held fixed, and thereby builds the
distribution of macro-F1 that this architecture attains when no
systematic relationship between the plant features and the label is left.
The p-value is the share of those 200 permutations that matched or
exceeded the value observed on the real labels. In each figure the grey
histogram is that null distribution, the solid red line the observed
value, and the dashed blue line the pooled nested cross-validation
estimate reported in @tbl-perf; the latter is the more conservative of
the two, because it re-tunes the model inside every fold instead of
holding one architecture fixed.

![Permutation test for the target variable valence: null distribution of the pooled macro-F1 over 200 label permutations for Random Forest on the session-normalized features, against the observed value. None of the 200 permutations reached it (p = 0.005).](figures/permutation_valence.png){#fig-perm-valence width=85%}

![Permutation test for the target variable arousal: null distribution of the pooled macro-F1 over 200 label permutations for the Neural Network on the session-normalized features, against the observed value. Ten of the 200 permutations matched or exceeded it (p = 0.055), so this target misses the conventional significance threshold.](figures/permutation_arousal.png){#fig-perm-arousal width=85%}

![Permutation test for the target variable emotion: null distribution of the pooled macro-F1 over 200 label permutations for Random Forest on the raw features, against the observed value. Two of the 200 permutations matched or exceeded it (p = 0.015).](figures/permutation_emotion.png){#fig-perm-emotion width=85%}

## Code Availability {#sec-appendix-code}

Every component described in this paper is hosted at

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\url{https://github.com/JakobJetter/COIN2026_Team-1_Plant-Emotion-Detector}
\end{center}
```

The repository is organised along the pipeline stages of @fig-pipeline.
The `arduino/` directory holds the ESP32 firmware that samples the
AD8232 and the CO~2~ sensor and streams both over WebSocket. The
notebooks under `notebooks/` then run in numeric order:
`01_init_recording` records one session into a shared event log and a
video file, `02_emotion_labelling` derives the per-window HRV, FER and
plant features and applies the labeling rule of
@sec-labeling-algorithm, `03_dataset_creation` runs that labeling over
every session and merges the result into the consolidated dataset, and
the three `04_*_ml_pipeline` notebooks train and compare the
classifiers for emotion, arousal and valence respectively.
`05_correlation_analysis` performs the CO~2~ confound analysis reported
in @sec-results. The live dashboard of @sec-live-demonstration is
implemented in `emotion_live_dashboard.py` under `phaenomena/`. The
consolidated dataset and the correlation result tables ship under
`data/datasets/`, so the modelling and correlation notebooks can be
re-run without repeating the recordings.
